issues.body: Section 4c states that backfill-provenance.parse_head_ref reads the same shape as worker-pr.WORKER_HEAD_RE and recommends importing WORKER_HEAD_RE as the sole worker-PR identifier. That is factually false in this checkout: worker-pr.WORKER_HEAD_RE accepts any safe suffix after `sparq-agent/issue-<N>-`, while backfill-provenance.py defines its own anchored HEAD_RE requiring exactly `issue-<N>-<run_id>-<attempt>`. A same-repository PR can therefore match WORKER_HEAD_RE without belonging to the provenance-producing worker population. The document's own argument against duplicated grammars does not establish that the broader classifier is the authoritative producer predicate. Using it can add non-record-bearing PRs to the manifest and cause permanent false gaps/refusals, so the recommended generator is not correct or complete as specified.
issues.fix_hint: Define the expected population from the actual provenance producer/recovery admission contract. Reconcile the two existing regexes explicitly (and any required same-repo/actor or run-binding conditions), identify one authoritative predicate only if it exactly characterizes record-bearing worker PRs, and add positive/negative cases showing that every admitted PR should have a provenance record while lookalike branches are excluded. If conservative over-enumeration is intentional, state and justify that operational tradeoff rather than claiming the shapes are identical.
issues.title: Proposed worker-PR population uses the wrong branch grammar

verdict.summary: The central independence argument is sound, but the proposed population predicate is not grounded in the actual producer grammar. The record says worker PRs should be identified solely with worker-pr.WORKER_HEAD_RE and claims backfill reads the same shape; the checkout shows that backfill uses a separate, materially narrower HEAD_RE requiring issue/run/attempt numeric components. The broader regex is also used as a general worker-lane classifier, not proof that a PR was produced by the provenance-writing workflow. Because this predicate defines the expected-record population, the design must reconcile the real producer/recovery predicates before it is safe to implement.
